name: HECS-HELP and Commonwealth supported places
summary: A government-subsidised uni place, plus a loan that covers your share of the fees so you pay nothing upfront.
key: HELP borrowing limit for most students: $129,883 (2026).
who: Australian citizens who study part of the course in Australia.
Some non-citizens resident in Australia, such as New Zealand Special Category Visa and permanent humanitarian visa holders.
need: A tax file number, or proof you have applied for one.
The Request for Commonwealth support and HECS-HELP form (eCAF) from your provider.
how: Check the course is offered as a Commonwealth supported place, on your uni's site or Course Seeker.
Apply for the course. Your offer letter says whether it is a supported place and how to accept.
Submit the eCAF through your provider on or before the census date.
Enrol in your units, then pay upfront or defer to HECS-HELP by the census date.
Check your balance any time on myHELPbalance.
catches: If you don't pay or defer by the census date, your supported-place enrolment is cancelled.
It covers tuition only, not rent, laptops or textbooks.
Eligibility for non-citizens depends on your visa. Check the Study Assist page for yours.

source.label: Study Assist: 2026 CSP and HECS-HELP fact sheet
